payload.why: the estate's chain has been on a memory-stream carrying a body kind since before tonight, which §7.2 forbids. Every frame sealed onto it made the eventual migration one frame bigger — 98 when I found it, 100 by the time I noticed I was still adding to it.
payload.what_this_is: a NEW body-stream on the estate's own rappid, bare as §7.2 requires. It is NOT a §12.1 re-genesis: that is one owner-authorized operation with sig != null, and I do not have the key and will not fabricate one. This line simply cites the old one and continues here.
payload.what_this_is_not: authority to retire the old chain. The legacy line stays exactly where it is, append-only and untouched, and remains the record of generations 1 through 35 until its owner converges it properly.
payload.for_the_owner: when you hold a key: §12.1 step 1 seals the legacy head's exact octets, step 2 emits a signed body.re-genesis at seq 0 carrying migrated_from, step 3 registers it and deprecates the prior genesis, step 4 moves the old frames under legacy/. tools/check_rapp1.py will go quiet the moment that lands.

payload.why: the word was tested and it failed the only test that matters for a vocabulary. Six cold readers — a skeptic, a schoolteacher, a game developer, a product manager, a researcher and a fifteen-year-old — all got the direction RIGHT after reading the page, 6/6. And all six volunteered, unprompted, that the word had fought them: 'my first guess was exactly backwards', 'the one place the everyday word actively misled me', 'a divergence operator wearing the name of a convergence operator', 'honestly I think braid is a bad name for it — every real braid I've ever seen makes things more together, not less'.
payload.the_rule_that_decided_it: I had set the rule 'rename only if it still fails', and by that rule braid survived — the page corrected it successfully. The rule was wrong. The sharper test is the one the flood argument implies: does it survive being half-remembered by somebody who read it once? A word that costs a correction every single time it is taught does not. Every other word in the vocabulary carried itself; this one needed an escort.
payload.why_cross_and_select: the operation is selective breeding, so the words are the breeder's: you CROSS many ways, then you SELECT what is furthest from both parents. They arrive as a pair, each carries its own meaning, and they hold hands with seed, fertile and grow — the family the estate was already using.
payload.kept: braid and plait remain as aliases. Renaming a thing should not break what calls it, and the old names are on a sealed frame at generation 32 which stands as it was written.
payload.unchanged_by_the_rename: the measurement. Six routes crossed and selected still reach 25.0% novel against the best single route's 19.4%, and every route still contributes something no other found.
